newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapores shares end higher as blue chips surge.
newsitem.headline: Singapores shares end higher as blue chips surge.

text.p: Singapore blue chips led a 1.7 percent surge on the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) on Monday as a major U.S. buying programme sparked a revival of the lacklustre market, dealers said.
"This kind of surge is something we haven't seen for a little while -- it's a welcome return," one dealer said.
"A bullish outlook is coming back to the market with U.S. funds correcting their underweighting," another dealer said.
The STII gained 35.27 points, or 1.7 percent, to end Monday at 2,101.48. Market volume was an active 202.4 million shares producing 188 gainers to 184 losers.
Hot news of the buy programme helped Singapore Press foreign stock and City Developments, both up Singapore $0.70 to S$29.00 and S$13.40 respectively.
Singapore Airlines foreign shares also took off, hitting an intra-day high of S$13.50 before landing up S$0.60 at S$13.30.
Newly listed Popular Holdings topped the actives with 15 million units traded, ending the day down a cent at S$0.51.
Losers were led by the Thai Prime investment fund, down US$0.45 at US$9.00, while construction counter Hong Fok saw its shares drop S$0.29 to S$2.97 on moderate volume.
